lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON.

instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Show me exactly how my film's soundtrack will be mixed: the music bed and how loud it is when, every voice line and every sound effect at its time, before anything is rendered", and give it nothing more: every input is optional.
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:plan-a-motion-films-soundtrack-premix and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Reads a motion film's cue sheet (its length, voice line offsets, the stretches where a voice is heard, and every sound effect as [time, palette sound, gain in dB]) and the film's settings, and answers the ffmpeg commands that premix its soundtrack: the music bed trimmed from its start and shaped over time (ducked while a voice is heard, set or lifted in named windows, faded out), each voice line delayed to its offset, each effect delayed to its time at its gain, all summed, then the film's loudness pass (in the graph, a measured gain and a limiter, or a linear two-pass loudnorm).
4. It reads and writes only its own rows through the records door: record:setting (records:read).

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
